title: Gauntlet proof 1 reads PASS when no driven turn was observed
body:
## Summary
evaluate_proof passes 'zero breaches' whenever nothing breached and something was driven, so a run whose every turn errored before the gate was read (no world, a driver fault) reports PASS with 0 held.

## Description
src/athena/proving/gauntlet/run.py:533 sets `"pass": not breached and bool(driven)`; `driven` (run.py:529) is every non-skipped result, and drive() returns verdict `error` with no TurnRecord when the world cannot be built (run.py:424-440) or the driver raises (run.py:470-478). So 'driven' includes turns whose gate was never read. The `bool(driven)` guard shows the intent that an empty run cannot pass; an all-error run is as empty. quality-gates/gate-liveness (failure-not-empty-success) and quality-gates/unmeasurable-criteria (absence that is the gate's own vision must not read as a pass). Fixed looks like: proof 1 passes only over observed turns (held or breached, or error turns that carry a record), and a run with none says n/a or FAIL with the reason; the CLI (src/athena/proving/__main__.py:190-209) and the trigger page (src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:442) render that state.

## Flow
- run_gauntlet with an Engines.world that raises OSError for every attack
- drive() -> every result {verdict: error, detail: 'world: OSError'}
- evaluate_proof -> {pass: True, breached: 0, held: 0, errors: 6, driven: 6}
- report.md: '1. **Zero breaches** - PASS: 0 breached, 0 held, 6 errors over 6 driven turns.'; __main__ exits 0

## Expected impact
A reader of a proving report (README 'Proof 1, zero breaches: pass') could be shown PASS for a run that observed no gate at all; measured by the probe below going from PASS to not-PASS. Could break: a hosted run with a few world errors and many held turns must still pass.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - proof 1 never passes on zero observed turns
Before: probe this round (scratchpad probe_vacuous.py, real run_gauntlet, n=2): pass True, held 0, errors 6 of 6 driven
After: same probe: pass not True (n/a or False with a reason); a run with held turns unchanged
Method: probe - the Before is measured; the After needs the consumers in proving-core (__main__ exit and print) and proving-hosted-server (page chip) changed with it, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: src/athena/proving/gauntlet/run.py:529-533 `driven = [r for r in results if not r.get("skipped")]` ... `"pass": not breached and bool(driven)`; run.py:424-440 world failure -> verdict error, no record. Probe output: {'pass': True, 'breached': 0, 'driven': 6, 'held': 0, 'errors': 6}; markdown '1. **Zero breaches** - PASS: 0 breached, 0 held, 6 errors over 6 driven turns.'
instrument: a run_gauntlet test whose world factory always raises: proof 1 must not read PASS; plus the __main__ exit code and the trigger page chip for that state

title: Characters: Nemotron purse has no judge reserve, so a spent purse reads as a kill
body:
## Summary
The Claude purse keeps 30% back for the Haiku judges, the Nemotron purse keeps nothing back for the Nemotron judge, so users and Athena-on-Nemotron can spend it and proof 2 then reports the Nemotron judge 'not used' as a kill.

## Description
src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:500 `limits = {CLAUDE: config.claude_cap * config.claude_athena_share}`: only the Claude row is held back, for the reason run.py:106-109 gives ('a row that spent the whole purse would leave both proofs unmeasured'). The simulated users (Nemotron) and Athena-on-Nemotron draw the NEMOTRON purse with no limit, and the Nemotron rubric judge runs last on the same purse (run.py:680-688). When it is spent the judge returns budget_exhausted (run.py:580-581), agreement has 0 pairs, rho None, and run.py:723-724 reports `killed: True`, `nemotron_judge: 'not used'`. ADR 0034 counts rho None as a kill for zero variance; here it is zero data. One rule (keep the judges' reserve) implemented for one purse of two. eval-harness/eval-economics, quality-gates/unmeasurable-criteria.

## Flow
- run_characters, claude_row off, three Characters, turns 3, nemotron_cap 0.03
- conversations spend 0.03 of 0.03 (2 of 3 complete)
- judge:rubric:lightning -> budget_exhausted; agreement pairs 0, rho None
- proof: killed True, nemotron_judge 'not used' (README/report: 'kill below 0.3')

## Expected impact
A small-cap or hosted Characters run would publish 'Nemotron as a judge: not used' as if it had failed the agreement bar; measured by pairs > 0 (or an 'unmeasured' state) at the same cap. Could break: the Claude row's share semantics if the reserve is generalised carelessly.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the Nemotron judge always gets to run, or the proof says unmeasured
Before: probe this round (scratchpad probe_reserve.py): cap 1.0 -> pairs 21 rho 1.0 usable; cap 0.03 -> pairs 0 rho None killed True 'not used'
After: at cap 0.03: the conversations stop at a Nemotron share, the judge scores, pairs > 0; or the proof reads unmeasured, not killed
Method: probe - Before measured on the real run; the After is a design choice (a NEMOTRON share in limits, and ADR 0034's None-is-a-kill for zero data) not taken in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:500 `limits = {CLAUDE: config.claude_cap * config.claude_athena_share}`; run.py:723-724 `"killed": rho is None or rho < AGREEMENT_KILL, "nemotron_judge": "not used" if rho is None ...`; probe: `0.03 pairs 0 rho None killed True not used spent 0.03 complete 2` vs `1.0 pairs 21 rho 1.0 killed False usable`
instrument: test_characters: run_characters with nemotron_cap=0.03, three Characters, claude_row off -> assert the agreement has pairs or reads unmeasured, never killed with 0 pairs

title: The playbook bench's cap ignores turns with no price, so it never binds on them
body:
## Summary
run_bench stops a run when its known spend passes cap_usd, but a turn whose cost is None adds nothing, so on an unpriced model the cap never binds; the same rule the proving purse breaks (proving-core card), at a second site.

## Description
src/athena/proving/playbooks/bench.py:269 `if run.cost > config.cap_usd:` and bench.py:319-323 add only a known cost (`if cost is None: run.cost_known = False else: run.cost += cost`). A Token Factory model not in the price table costs None (src/athena/harness/tokenfactory.py:135-137), and `bench --engine nebius --model <any>` is free text (src/athena/proving/playbooks/__main__.py:78-79). The run stays bounded by turns (phases x (MAX_CONTINUATIONS+1) x (nudges+1) + follow-ups), so this is a dead cap, not an unbounded spend. Pair of the proving-core card 'An unpriced or failed role call costs nothing in the purse, so the cap never binds' (budget.py), which does not name this site. eval-harness/eval-economics.

## Flow
- bench <id> --engine nebius --model <a model absent from PRICES> --cap 0.01
- every turn's ledger cost_usd None -> run.cost stays 0.0
- the cap check never fires; the report says cost_usd null

## Expected impact
Whoever benches an unpriced model with a cap believes the cap holds; measured as turns run after the cap under a no-price model_fn. Could break: a priced run's stopping point if unknown cost is counted pessimistically.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the bench cap binds or refuses when the cost is unknown
Before: code reading: bench.py:269 and :319-323; tokenfactory.py:135-137 returns None for an unpriced model
After: a run_bench test with a model_fn reporting no cost and cap 0 stops (or refuses to start) before a second turn
Method: simulation - three walked cases (priced claude_code: binds; unpriced nebius: never binds; failed turn: run ends on its error anyway); not probed this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/playbooks/bench.py:269 `if run.cost > config.cap_usd:`; bench.py:319-323 `cost = record.cost_usd / if cost is None: run.cost_known = False / else: run.cost += cost`; src/athena/harness/tokenfactory.py:135-137 `price = PRICES.get(model) / if price is None:` (returns None)
instrument: test_playbooks: run_bench with a world whose scripted model reports cost None and BenchConfig(cap_usd=0.0) -> count world.turn calls; decide whether unknown cost refuses the cap or counts turns

title: Characters: after the users escalate, the rows report only the Super pass's cost and turns
body:
## Summary
When fidelity fails on Lightning the whole plan is conversed again on Super and the report's rows and conversations are rebuilt from the second pass only, so Athena's turns and cost from the first pass vanish from every row while the purse and the ledger count both.

## Description
src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:662 `conversations = converse_all(plan, "super", ...)` replaces the list; run.py:750 `"rows": _rows(conversations, config)` and run.py:762 `"conversations": [...]` read only it; users[0] (run.py:650) keeps the first pass's fidelity line but no row keeps its Athena spend. `cost_usd` (run.py:763) and `cost_by_role` (run.py:764) come from the budget and the ledger, which saw both passes, so the report disagrees with itself.

## Flow
- run_characters with a control that judges every user turn out of persona (escalation to Super)
- row athena-claude: athena_turns 4, cost_usd 0.008
- cost_by_role['athena:athena-claude'] 0.016; report conversations: 1 (the Super pass)

## Expected impact
A reader comparing rows to the run's cost sees half the Athena spend; measured as rows' cost against the ledger's athena role after an escalation. Could break: the desktop/hosted readers of rows if a second row per rung is added.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every Athena turn and dollar a run spent is in a row
Before: probe this round (scratchpad probe_escalate.py): rows cost 0.008, 4 turns; ledger athena cost 0.016
After: rows (or a per-rung row) account for 0.016 and 8 turns
Method: probe - Before measured; the shape of the After (fold both passes, or one row per user rung) is a reporting decision this round did not take
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/characters/run.py:662 `conversations = converse_all(plan, "super", engines, caller, budget, log, config)`; run.py:750 `"rows": _rows(conversations, config)`; probe: `rows: planned 1 athena_turns 4 cost 0.008` vs `ledger athena cost 0.016 conversations in report 1 users ['lightning', 'super']`
instrument: test_characters: test_a_failed_fidelity_proof_escalates_the_users_to_super_once extended to assert sum of row cost_usd == cost_by_role['athena:athena-claude']
